newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX closes record-breaking session higher.
newsitem.headline: German DAX closes record-breaking session higher.

text.p: German shares ended a busy bourse session on Friday just shy of record highs, with the DAX index of 30 German blue-chips ending the day a full percentage point higher.

A combination of factors prompted the more bullish mood in Frankfurt, notably the stronger dollar, firmer Bunds and the 0.30 percent higher overnight close on Wall Street and the DAX ended the day at points, up.
The DAX hit a bourse all-time high of 2,597.73 points earlier on before closing at 2,595.96, one percent or 25.64 points higher.
Traders said U.S. consumer prices and retail sales data due at 1230 GMT could have a big impact on trade, as the market is watching closely for signs of inflationary pressure there.
Some traders said further gains could be limited. "I don't think there is enough impetus to break out of the current ranges just yet," said one trader.
Others, however, said the continued strength of the dollar could be enough to push the DAX index over the psychologically-important 2,600 point threshold.
Chemical stocks led the market in terms of number of shares traded, but they registered mixed performances.

BASF AG ended up 73 pfennigs at 45.80 marks and Bayer AG was up 60 pfennigs at 54.87 marks, but Hoechst AG was down 24 pfennigs at 53.70 marks, amid scepticism that its AgrEvo unit would achieve its forecast sales target.
Deutsche Bank AG continued its rally of recent days after Thursday's confirmation that UBS investment bank had upgraded Deutsche and its shares ended bourse up 55 pfennigs at 72.15 marks.
